newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Cariplo cuts lending rates.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Cariplo cuts lending rates.

text.p: Italy's Cassa di Risparmio delle Provincie Lombarde (Cariplo) said it was cutting its prime rate to 9.5 percent from 10.0 percent and top rate to 16.0 from 17.0 percent, effective from January 1.
Cariplo said in a statement it had decided to reduce its lending rates in line with the market trend.
Several major banks decided to cut their rates earlier this month following calls for lower lending rates from Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio.
The prime rate is the rate at which banks lend to their best customers and the top rate is the ceiling rate at which they lend to clients.
